obernants.approximation_semantics: Proposed inner bound of absent behavior under the stated premises; source-derived and checked on finite fixtures, not proved for all Rust executions.
obernants.assumptions: Lawful ordering/cloning where required, standard Rust and successful allocation.
obernants.domain: Implementations paired with finite test outcomes.
obernants.operator: In the universe of implementations and test outcomes, any passing implementation that disagrees with an asserted sampled oracle equality is excluded, assuming faithful assertions. Unsampled bugs may still pass.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived relation; bounded executable evidence only, no unrestricted proof.
obernants.assumptions: Lawful ordering/cloning where required, standard Rust and successful allocation.
obernants.domain: Implementations paired with finite test outcomes.
obernants.operator: A pass reconstructs the set of implementations agreeing on all sampled observations; a failure reconstructs those violating at least one assertion. Neither observation uniquely recovers implementation or universal correctness.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived conditional relation with finite executed checks; no unrestricted semantic proof.
obernants.assumptions: Lawful total ordering; value-preserving independent clones where required; source-bound tests; no panics, overflow or allocation failure.
obernants.domain: The exact finite fixtures and assertions in this test source, with the production implementation under test.
obernants.observation_scope: Operation observations or finite traces explicitly specified by the relation.
obernants.operator: Passing requires the declared production observations to satisfy their decomposition, transport, containment, simultaneous-fiber and order relations on every enumerated fixture. Premises are checked separately by explicit counterexamples. Relations may miss correlated errors, so independent scan checks remain necessary.

obernants.observation_scope: Operation observations or finite traces explicitly specified by the relation.
obernants.operator: Observation of the non-strict order-collapse counterexample excludes extending strict order-embedding claims to merely monotone maps. Index-only observations retain ambiguous value preimages. Passing these assertions constrains the claims on these concrete inputs; it does not establish their maximal domains.

obernants.operator: The finite test suite partitions implementations into accepted and rejected sets. The recorded compiled production mutant belongs to the rejected set at a named correspondence assertion. This is sensitivity to that defect, not completeness for all defects or a general proof of the model.
